chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Starting to arrange in 1928; Sy Oliver and writing at piano
summary: Smith began arranging seriously in 1928 in Little Rock, admired Sy Oliver with Andy Kirk, and writes at the piano.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When did you start doing arranging seriously?
Oh, I started in 1928. Yeah, 1928. We was in Little Rock at the ...(?)..., and I was writing it up for everybody. I was the only arranger in the band. I had to do all of it.
Now, by 1928, were the Blue Devils unusual in having arrangements like this? Or were all the bands doing it?
Yes. All the bands was doing it. All of them. The next great man to come down was with the Clouds of Joy -- Sy Oliver. You ever heard of him?
Sy Oliver. Sure, I know Sy.

Yeah, great arranger. Yeah, he got with Andy Kirk and them, and he was writing some great arrangements in there. The boys come in and say, "Boy, old Sy... We were listening to Andy Kirk and them last night, and old Sy Oliver's over there. He's a new man, from Ohio or somewhere." They said, "He's got some great arrangements." So I used to go listen to him. I'd be at home somewhere, sitting up writing music. So I'd go over and hear him.
When you were writing music, did you used to work it out on piano first?
Yes. I still do it on piano. That's where I get my effects(?).
Some people are amazing. Some people can do it without...
Yeah, that's what Eddie Durham do.
He can sit down with a piece of paper and do it.
Yeah. Benny Carter says it slows him up. He don't fool with no piano.
